# Draft:Leah (software)

}}
Leah (formerly ContractPodAi) is a London-based legal technology company that develops contract lifecycle management (CLM) software and related artificial intelligence tools for enterprise legal departments and other business functions.
History
ContractPod Technologies Limited, the legal entity behind ContractPodAi, was incorporated on 6 June 2012, though sources differ on when the company began trading, with some reporting 2012, and others 2015.
In July 2019, the company disclosed a US$55 million Series B funding round led by Insight Partners, as part of a period of increased investment in contract lifecycle management software.
Reuters announced the company raised US$115 million Series C investment in September 2021, led by the SoftBank Vision Fund, the first time the fund had invested in a legal technology company. In 2023, the company introduced an AI legal assistant under the name "Leah".
In January 2026, ContractPodAi rebranded as Leah, aligning the company name with its AI platform brand name.
Products and platform
The company's core product is an AI-powered contract lifecycle management platform. In 2019, the platform's scope spanned contract generation, a contract repository, and third-party review workflows, with AI functionality built using IBM Watson. By 2023 the platform had integrated ChatGPT and other AI tools.
The Financial Times included ContractPodAi in a special report on how artificial intelligence tools were reducing friction in legal and contracting workflows, noting the company's partnership strategy with legal services providers and professional services firms.
The company expanded beyond contract lifecycle management with a broader platform allowing in-house legal teams to manage different types of legal matters.
In 2022, ContractPodAi launched a legal intake application intended to automate and triage requests for in-house legal departments.
In 2026, the Leah platform became the company's primary AI platform offering, marketed for use by legal teams and other corporate departments. PwC also announced a partnership with ContractPodAi to use its platform for contract management.
